Review Title: Misfortune turned into a very happy day thanks to SeaWind
Review Text:
After my cruise ship floatplane excursion, a long-awaited journey for a special birthday treat, was cancelled due 'high winds', something that wasn't apparent that warm and sunny afternoon, especially as the floatplanes kept taking off and landing right next to the ships, including the company that was doing my cancelled excursion, I then quickly shopped around onshore for a replacement flight with limited shore-time left.

Two attempted bookings failed - someone scored a last seat just before me, and another company couldn't find enough passengers to make it worthwhile. Thankfully the remaining one, SeaWind Aviation, had room for me on my preferred aircraft - an original radial engined DHC-2 Beaver. As a retired airline pilot, it was Beavers flying overhead as a small kid that helped seed my interest in aviation.

Not only was SeaWind less expensive than the cancelled cruise ship excursion, but I got picked up from the ship by co-owner Lesley, driven a very short distance to their terminal and dock facilities, and soon after was sitting up the front right behind that rumbling radial engine - marvellous!

The pilot, Mike, not only handled the Beaver on water and in the air like a maestro but removed all the bumps that had been responsible for the previous flight's 'cancellation'. I suspect overbooking was the real reason for that, but I was so fortunate to fall into the friendly care of Lesley and Mike from SeaWind, and that marvellous old, shiny and obviously well-maintained Beaver.

The flight not only took in the advertised sightseeing around Ketchikan harbour, but went well off along valleys, between forested mountains and across several islands to make ripples on a perfectly smooth isolated island lake, landing and taking off just for fun :)

Headsets and an intercom allowed Mike to answer passengers' questions along the way. We returned to Ketchikan, landing right beside the cruise ships and tying up at the dock about 150m from my ship - an easy walk back, sporting a new 'Beaver' cap, rather than trouble Lesley for another ride :)

I'm still grinning at the memory of that ride and so proud of my 'birthday' hat :)

Review Title: Der Schein hat uns getrogen, wir fühlen uns belogen!
Review Text:
Unsere Buchung über Travelstart war:
Hinflug - Stuttgart – Zürich – Mumbai – GOA,
Rückflug - GOA – Mumbai – München - Stuttgart

Wir waren sehr zufrieden mit der Abwicklung unserer Flugbuchung.
Auch war die Information über die Flugzeiten und die Zeiten bis zu den nächsten Flügen so angegeben, das wir keine Probleme bei den Transfers zum jeweils nächsten Flug zu befürchten hatten.
Am Flughafen Stuttgart wurde uns beim Aufgeben des Gepäcks gesagt, dass wir das Gepäck in Mumbai abholen und neu aufgeben müssten.
Die dafür zur Verfügung stehende Zeit von dreieinhalb Stunden haben wir als ausreichend angesehen.
In Mumbai angekommen hatten wir an der Immigration reichlich lange zu warten und nach der Immigration waren noch weitere zeitaufwändige Kontrollen .
Die Abholung der Koffer ist nach der Immigration und wir waren so spät, das wir die Koffer nicht mehr vom Band holen konnten, sondern an der Stelle abholen mussten wo die nicht abgeholten Koffer deponiert waren.
Als wir die Koffer wieder aufgeben wollten, war das Boarding bereits geschlossen.
In der Folge waren wir gezwungen, einen anderen Flug nach GOA zu suchen.
Wir konnten dann einen Flug buchen, der erst am Abend stattfand, also mehr als 19 Stunden später, zusätzliche Kosten ca. 150 €.
Natürlich war unser Taxifahrer, den wir bereits organisiert hatten, umsonst von Arambol nach Mumbai gefahren, Kosten 3.000 lNR, ca. 34 €.

In den Statuten von Travelstart steht:

„Wenn Sie ein Rückflugticket haben, ist es nicht möglich, den Hinflug verfallen zu lassen und nur den Rückflug zu nutzen.
Flugtickets müssen in chronologischer Reihenfolge verwendet werden, da die Fluggesellschaft ansonsten den verbleibenden Teil der Reise storniert.“

Trotz stundenlanger Chats über mehrere Tage ist es uns nicht gelungen, Travelstart zu überzeugen, dass wir den Flug von Mumbai nach GOA ohne eigenes Verschulden versäumt hatten.

Organisation für den Rückflug:
Den über Travelstart gebuchten Rückflug am 21.12. 2022 von GOI nach STR,
Flugnummern UK 844 GOI - BOM,
LH 767 BOM - MUC,
LH 2144 MUC - STR
konnten wir nicht antreten, da der Hinflug nicht komplett durchgeführt wurde - was nicht unser Verschulden war - und wir trotz wiederholtem Chat mit den Mitarbeitern von Travelstart keine Freigabe für den gebuchten und bezahlten Rückflug bekommen haben.

Somit waren wir gezwungen, einen anderen Rückflug zu buchen.
Die Daten: QR 523 GOI - DOH 22.12.2022 04:05 am
QR 71 DOH - FRA 22.12.2022 02:00 pm
Zusätzliche Kosten 90.030 lNR, ca. 1.028 €

Die Strecke Frankfurt - Stuttgart wurde mittels privatem PKW organisiert.

Die Summe der zusätzlichen obigen Kosten beträgt 1.213 € (ohne Berücksichtigung der Abholung durch privaten PKW aus Frankfurt).

Ein Schreiben an Travelstart über die unbefriedigende Abwicklung der Buchung blieb bisher unbeantwortet!

Review Title: Wonderful flight experience over Alaskan mountains!
Review Text:
We booked a seaplane flight and water landing (for an extra fee) with SeaWind directly after comparing to other similar opportunities online. Lesley and company did a fine job from the get-go, communicating with us throughout the process, to the morning of our flight, until we were dropped off just feet from our ship. Part of her difficult job was delaying our flight an hour, then telling us that we would not be able to fly over Misty Fjords and visit the monument due to cloud cover and flight conditions. Instead of cancelling the flight, we were offered another, sure to be beautiful, instead. We accepted.

Our pilot Anthony was fantastic; a local who loved flying, was excited to take us over an area they rarely get to fly over with a group, and told personal stories along the way. The "lake landing" was the highlight, bending into a postcard-like scene to the (unplanned) song "Paradise". The landing was soft and serene, we were able to get off the plane (one in our party even took a icy swim) for an all-too-short but sweet visit. We saw mountains, valleys, peaks, waterfalls, and tried to spot animals, milking every moment. Headsets were used as my wife interviewed a patient and thoughtful Anthony from her shotgun seat. It was a smooth, beautiful flight we will remember forever. Thank you SeaWind for a great experience from start to finish.

If we had to nit-pick, the only glitch may be that as we eagerly waited to board the plane, some in the other party we flew with still had to register and pay, perhaps delaying our flight, which, due to weather, was already an hour+ behind schedule. We still got a full tour as promised, but felt a bit rushed at the end due to a short 4 hour Ketchikan visit. 5 stars.

Super sad, we decided to just spend the day walking around Ketchikan and I was going to drown my sorrows by eating King Crab. I mean sounded redeeming….anyways. We spent the morning wandering around town, and after about two hours found ourselves back at the visitor center. We went in to see if there were any tours and voila! Another flight seeing tour! We booked it. We then waited until the time to go, boarded the van, and then….cancelled. It’s windy apparently.

Sadder than we were before, we just started walking across town. Full bags on camera gear in tow…we walked. And stopped and ate crab. And then we walked. And then!!!! Haha We found an eagle!!! Just sitting there. Good sign right? And then we found more eagles, and so we just kept following the eagles, until we reached Seawind Aviation. It looked closed, but I walked in. No one was there. I jiggled the little bells on the door, and moments later the kindest people appeared. I asked if there were any seaplane tours, and they were like “sure!! We have one that can go at 13:30?” We jumped on it, and the rest was history! The third time really is the charm and saved us from leaving Ketichikan a little bit sadder. We could not have asked for a better experience.

We had a wonderful time! Highly, highly recommend them. Steve - our pilot - has been flying in this area for over 30 years. Could not have asked for a better experience.

Oh. And those eagles we followed….all apparently hang out at Seawind Aviation. 🥰🤗 It was just meant to be for us, and we could not have had a better day. Sometimes things just work out as they should and birds always know the way. 😉

Review Text:
I booked a trip to Traitor's Cove directly from the website, which was pretty easy to navigate, and received confirmation of the booking within 24 hours (it might have been closer to 10 hours).

The directions in terms of where to meet were very clear (by the berth next to our cruise ship's), and the vans were clearly marked and easy to find. It was a short drive to the Seawind office/dock.

We flew in one of the 7 passenger De Havillands. It was surprisingly comfortable. We spent a few minutes figuring out seating, which did worry me. (What if someone lied about their weight and they balanced the plane incorrectly?) However, the flight went very smoothly and we were able to see a lot of the Tongass National Forest on our way to Traitor's Cove. On the way back, one of the kids decided he wanted my seat (to be closer to his little brother), and so we switched with no discernible difference as to the smoothness of the flight. I guess the weight balancing didn't need to be that precise!

Our plane had two-way headsets which the kids tested out. The flight itself was somewhere between 20-30 minutes long. Our pilot provided commentary on the way out, but gave us time to just look out and relax on the way back.

After the flight, we took a short drive, and then a short walk to the viewing platform. Along the way, our guide reiterated the bear viewing/safety guidelines, and pointed out native plants and fresh bear scat.

We were the first group of the day to arrive at the viewing platform, where the USFS ranger pointed out a bear who was already fishing for salmon. In all, we saw 7 bears (or maybe 8?), including one who walked right under our platform, and a mama bear fishing with her two cubs. We also saw salmon jumping, and two bald eagles. We stayed for about 2 hours - one group arrived and left while we were there, and another arrived about 30 minutes before we left. During that time, the platform was never crowded, and there was plenty of space for everyone to get a good view. My binoculars were handy at times, but not necessary, as most of the bears were very close.

This was an incredible experience! That being said, I understand that it is heavily dependent on Mother Nature's cooperation and I was lucky. We were told all flights the previous day had been cancelled due to the weather, and that viewing in July had been poor as the lack of rain had affected the salmon run. However, the easy communication, the smooth and scenic flight, and the friendly and knowledgeable guides made all the parts under human control excellent (and the bears were great as well :-)

Review Text:
My family went on this as an excursion during our Alaskan cruise. I had called a few months before and the customer service is great! They helped us plan out the best times according to the cruise schedule and even gave us a discount for our large group (10).

They gave me a call before we got off the cruise and I had their phone number on hand, just in case. When we got there, everyone was super friendly. We split into two groups and took two planes.

The scenery is just gorgeous! We flew between mountains and over several bodies of water. In one area, the pilot spotted orcas and landed our plane near them so we could get a closer look. It was such a unique experience. My nephew was super happy during this part. We later landed on a dock for a break and took some pictures in the Alaskan wilderness. My cousin spotted jellyfish here! When we took off again, we spotted bald eagles but were unable to see any bears this time around. Still, I was so happy we got to see the orcas at such a close range in the wild!

The only thing I would caution anyone about is motion sickness. The planes are small and you feel a lot of movement (especially when the plane turns). My nephew got sick but the pilot was prepared with bags and paper towels. He was very nice and understanding. The rest of us were fine. So, please make sure to take medicine if you need it!

Overall, I would definitely recommend this activity to others. You always hear about lots of wildlife in Alaska but it still surprises you when you actually see it. We also had great weather, so it was a memorable and fun time.

Review Title: Stuff Your Face & Fly With The Eagles
Review Text:
My trip began with a bus ride from the dock to the lodge (perhaps a half hour trip), then the crab feed, then a flight back to Ketchikan. Depending on when you go, the order may be reversed.

The trip up was on a comfortable bus, with a fun driver. Plenty of local color and stories.

Then the feast. As many dungeness crab legs as you want, with all the butter you want. Delicious. And messy. Dessert is cheesecake, but you can skip that and have more crab if you prefer.

The flight back was on a 1950s vintage Dehavilland Beaver with up to date avionics. Surprisingly short take off run. Then over the island to Ketchikan and a smooth landing. My first flight in such a small aircraft and it's a very different sort of experience. The trip is short, but fun with great views. And if you you are lucky, as I was on this trip, you can find yourself soaring with Bald Eagles over the forest.

I was afraid Leslie would not accept the cancellation or charge me a hefty fee, but she was incredibly helpful. She told me she understood and didn't want us to fly if we couldn't enjoy it. This is what customer service is all about! Often, we out-of-town folks get the short end of the stick, squeezed for our hard-earned dollars with overpriced activities. We also don't have control over the weather so we can be hesitant to book expensive activities dependent on good weather. But there are a few operators like SeaWind Aviation who will work with you.

Review Title: Cool flight, Beautiful Bears and great Guide
Review Text:
We were 8 people flying with 2 planes. The flight was very interesting to us, as this was the first time to take off from the water. The view were great, we saw deer, a bear and when we saw seals the pilot did a loop around them so we can see them clearly!
We landed in a spectacular bay and were greeted by 2 Bold Eagles. We had a van waited for us to the start of a short trail. The guide was great – he explained a lot about the bears and how we would walk along the path. We felt safe and were happy to have him with us . The hike itself was easy, pretty level, on a good path. Our first bear was few feet below us eating a salmon very actively, in the stream next to it you were able to see the salmons swim and spawn by. The next 3 bears we saw from a little distance – they were in the middle of the stream fishing – unfortunately, the guide continue, and was not willing to go back so we can see it properly  - We were very close to the viewing ramp – and he probably thought that we will see many bears there – but there were none – we waited an hour in the viewing platform and headed back – we didn’t see any no the way back.
In the viewing ramp we were able to see so many salmons jumping the water fall – it was amazing!

To conclude – if you can budget it – it is a great experience!!!
Notice! Bear viewing is not guarantee anywhere, so if you do see a bear, even from a distance, agree with your guide ahead of time that you would like to pause and watch…

(The bears photos and the jumping salmons i keep to myself...you should go and take them yourself ;-) )

Review Text: We were in port in Ketchikan for half a day on Friday 7/3 from the NCL Pearl and had booked an independent flightseeing excursion with Seawind based on the reviews on Trip Advisor.  SeaWind was excellent.  A week before the excursion, there was a horrible tragedy with another flightseeing company on an excursion near identical to ours in the Misty Fjords in Ketchikan that left the pilot and all 8 passengers aboard dead.  As you can imagine, this scared the heck out of my family and I, the news breaking the day before our flight to Seattle to board our Alaska cruise.  Well, we kept our reservation with SeaWind and am glad we did.  The owner Leslie picked us up from the port and she raised the issue of the accident and discussed it with us openly and candidly.  It really helped to set us at ease.  After we got to the office for our safety briefing, the mechanic reported the plane we were going to use needed a new starter.  Undeterred, Leslie had her employee drive us to Creek Street in Ketchikan to kill 45 mins so we didn't have to just sit there.  We probably would have missed the wonderfully quirky Creek Street otherwise, so this was an error that worked in our favor.  Once the plane was fixed, we were whisked back to Seawind (where we saw a bald eagle perched on the building in perfect view) and then taken to the plane.  While we were not able to do the full hour flight planned if we wanted to still do the crab feast (which we did), it was still an amazing and beautiful 25 min flight.   While our pilot Mike could have been a little more talkative in my opinion, he was still very good (albeit a little quiet).  My mom, son and I were the only 3 passengers so the ride was 100% private!  The weather was perfect -- around 70 with a gentle breeze and very few clouds.  The radio blared Tom Petty's Learning to Fly and some other really great tunes throughout the flight!  Leslie also discounted the price of the tour significantly to account for the delay and shorter flight, which was more than fair.  After we stuffed ourselves silly with Dungeness Crab at the George Inlet Lodge where the pilot dropped us, we took a bus with some other tourists back to town.  My mom couldn't bring her wheelchair on the plane, so Leslie met us back in town to bring it back to us.  Despite the little bumps in the road, Leslie and Seawind went the extra mile to keep us safe and make sure we were comfortable, satisfied and happy.  I can't recommend SeaWind highly enough!  Don't be scared -- just do it!  It is truly an experience of a lifetime.

Review Title: This is not a flightseeing review....
Review Text:
We didn't charter Seawind for a flightseeing tour, nor were we cruise ship passengers. We had something much more challenging for Seawind and the service and support we received was exceptional.

My wife and I are wilderness campers - Alaska is our favorite place for this but we had never been to southeast Alaska or the Ketchikan area. Planning a trip like this begins 9-12 months ahead, which is when Seawind first helped. Once we decided on the general area we wanted to go to - I contacted several air charter companies in Ketchikan asking for advice and recommendations. Steve and Lesley at Seawind were by far the most helpful and responsive. I talked to both during the winter and with their recommendations reserved National Forest Service cabins in two different locations for a week each. One in Misty Fjords National Monument and the other on Prince of Wales Island.

Seawind's communication was excellent during the planning phase. They recommended an outfitter, a satellite phone rental company, and even a saltwater fishing guide for the few days we had in Ketchikan between camping trips. All worked out excellently.

Once we arrived in Ketchikan, I hesitate to write how much Lesley and Steve helped us out, because they went so far above the expected I don't want to create the impression that everyone should expect the service we received. Suffice it to say - they treated us more like family guests than customers.

The actual trips went very well. They loaded all of our gear in the plane, we left promptly when planned and the flight was smooth and enjoyable. Steve explained scenic highlights along the way, helped us unload our gear and even provided fishing tips for our destination. Pickup a week later was exactly as scheduled, although this time Rolf was our pilot. Due to weather we had to take a different route than our trip in, but this was nice because we got to see different scenery, and Rolf took his time to explain highlights along the way. Rolf even took the time to tell us about some of the wildlife to expect at our second cabin ;) . My wife especially appreciated this information.

Our second trip out started as planned with the same great flight out, also with Rolf, to Prince of Wales Island. Arrival and unloading was smooth and efficient. On our day to leave the weather turned bad, with low fog and lots of rain. We were in contact with Seawind via our rented satellite phone, and they tried to make it in to land but had to turn back. Rolf waited in a nearby bay for three hours waiting hoping the weather would clear, but it didn't. We heard him try to get in several times, but the fog and clouds were just too thick to make it into our lake. We had a 9 am flight the next morning to Seattle. In a last attempt to get us to our flight on time Rolf tried again - at 5:30 a.m. to once again make it in - but the weather hadn't improved so he had to turn back. Finally in the middle of the afternoon, the weather cleared some, I called Seawind and Steve was on his way to get us. He made it in OK, we packed up and left, and caught our rescheduled airline flight the next day. I'm sure it was expensive to make three attempts for one pick up - but Seawind did not hesitate at all to try.

We have traveled to wilderness Alaska lakes with several other air charter companies - I have to say Seawind is the best. Their dedication to customers and safety is exemplary. The planes are equipped with modern avionics, very clean and appear to be well maintained. Both Steve and Rolf are excellent pilots, and know the area well. Lesley is fantastic - she runs the office, is available day and night, and can help with any local support you may need.

The next time we need a charter service in the Ketchikan area - Seawind will be our only choice.

Review Text:
This is a fantastic way to see the immensity of the Misty Fjords area. There is no way a land-based trip can give you the scope of the area that a small plane can, and SeaWind was a perfect company for my small family of three to go with to see the scenery. From pick-up to return, the entire process is very professional and friendly, with a true family feel to the experience. There were five people in our little sea plane, not counting the pilot, and we all had great views as all seats are alongside a window. We took off from the same harbor where our cruise ship was docked, and we flew over forests, mountains, lakes, waterfalls, and rivers. While we were in a plane, it was still easy for the pilot to get close to the areas he wanted us to see. For example, he circled around a waterfall a few times so we could all get a good view, and since the plane was so small and relatively slow moving, we all got up close and personal. It was amazing to see such pristine wilderness from the perfect vantage points. We took a ton of pictures out of the windows, and they looked really good. It's a great way to capture the sights.

Rolf, our pilot, gave us expert commentary as we went along, and he really knows his stuff after spending decades in the area. I was sitting in the front passenger seat, and he showed me the radar, communication equipment, and other cool cockpit stuff. It was really cool.

We landed on a beautiful lake for a short photo stop. I'm sure one of the pictures Rolf took of us will make it to our Christmas card this year. It was a gorgeous location and was about as peaceful as can be. Then we got back in the plane for the second half of the flight, which was as beautiful as the first. Rolf took us a different way back, which was great. We loved every minute of it.

The trip isn't cheap, but if you're in Ketchikan, do yourself a favor and splurge on a trip like this. If you do, go with SeaWind. They are great people who will give you a once-in-a-lifetime experience. You won't regret it for a minute.

All in all, it was a great adventure, well worth the cost (especially considering the savings over the cruise ship options) with over an hour of flight time! Review Title: No bears to be seen, but a Great Ride!
Review Text:
We wanted to do something really special and different while on our recent cruise to Alaska and thought a ride on a small plane to see bears in their natural habitat would be perfect.  As luck would have it, we were blessed with a warm, sunny day for our flight-seeing trip with Seawind Aviation to observe bears at Traitor's Cove.  

We were picked up as scheduled on the dock, driven to the DeHavilland Beaver 6-passenger floatplane, shown a brief safety video while we all settled our accounts, and led to the plane.  I have to say that I had been nervously anticipating this small-plane ride since the day we booked months ago, but the ease of getting my arthritic legs up and into the aircraft and the silky smooth takeoff melted away all my fears.  

After about 20 minutes of beautiful scenery, with pilot Steve narrating as we flew, we landed effortlessly at the dock, where a short walk brought us to the van that would drive us into the rainforest to a trail.  With some preliminary instruction in the event of a confrontation with a bear, we walked along the half-mile trail to an observation deck overlooking a creek, where we all had our eyes peeled for bears coming to feast on spawning salmon.  

Unfortunately, the unseasonably warm, dry, sunny weather - while great for the tourists - had not been good for bear sightings.  The water level in the creek was low, with fewer salmon, resulting in fewer bears.  Sadly, no bears were seen on this trip.  On the upside, we did see a bald eagle or two in the area which occupied our time for a time at the creek.  

Although we were disappointed that the bears did not come out to play, we still enjoyed the ride immensely and marveled at both the experience and the beautiful views it provided.  Owners Steve and Leslie run a nice business.  Leslie welcomed us warmly on arrival, and Steve provided a smooth, safe ride.  I would highly recommend them and hope to return one day for a ride over Misty Fjord.

Review Text:
If you want a first-class, personal, one-of-a-kind, floatplane experience while in Ketchikan, then SeaWind Aviation should be your first call.

First, the service offered by Lesley. Always so quick to respond to my e-mails. Due to unfortunate circumstances, the Alaskan cruise my husband and I were originally booked on was cancelled one week prior to our embarkation. We quickly got ourselves scheduled on a different cruiseship and cruiseline that would be in Ketchikan on a different day. Lesley was extremely accomodating in sliding our existing reservation to our new day with such short notice. Thank you for that! We knew exactly where we would be picked up. The instructions were very good and detailed. It is just a short drive from the cruise ship dock to their offices where the floatplanes wait.

We were fortunate to be in Ketchikan on one of the few days it does not rain. The sun was shining and Alaska was showing us her beauty. Our pilot seemed to genuinely enjoy this day for flying. We all had our headphones and microphones and could talk to each other freely throughout the flight. He gave us a wonderful tour of the Misty Fjords.

About half-way thru our flight, we touched down on a floating dock in the middle of the Fjords. We were joined by two other floatplanes. To see these planes take off and land was so much fun. Of course, it's even more fun to be in one as it takes off and lands. So smooth. It was nice to get out of the plane, stretch our legs, and take in the natural beauty that was surrounding us.

The second half of our tour in the air was just as stunning as the first half. It seemed we were being taken back to Ketchikan a different way so we could see more of the Misty Fjords. On our plane was a three-year-old. Our pilot was so kind to take into consideration his little ears. On our flight back to Ketchikan, he planned to gradually lower our flying elevation so that it would be easier for the pressure in the young child's ears. What kindness!

He also made sure we all had a good view of each of our cruiseships from the air. There were three ships in port that day. On our floatplane was the pilot, six adults and the three-year-old. We were passengers on two of the three ships so we each got a neat picture of our ship from the air.

If I have the opportunity to be in Ketchikan again, and I hope I do, my husband and I will book another excursion with SeaWind without hesitation. They make you feel like you are a part of their family. Because they are independent and do not have have contracts with the various cruise lines, you are guaranteed a more personal, tailored experience.

Thank you SeaWind for one of our top highlights of our 12-day vacation in Alaska and Canada!

Review Title: If you already cruised through Tracy Arm Fjord, I would skip this excursion.
Review Text:
SeaWind Aviation itself is a good company. I would not hesitate to recommend them if you really insist on taking a seaplane ride to Misty Fjord from Ketchikan. However, my review and rating is more about whether it is worth spending the money to go on this excursion if you came in on a cruise through the inside passage.

Like most people, we came on a cruise ship. I can't speak about the ship that cruised through Glacier National Park but if you cruised through Tracy Arm Fjord, the scenery is similar to that of Misty Fjord. With that said, I just don't see the value of going on this excursion. .

The take-off's and landing were very smooth. We didn't have a completely clear day but it wasn't terrible. Unfortunately, we did not see any wildlife that was mentioned on the website. We were really hoping to see some bears. I think that would have made the tour a bit more worthwhile. Of course, this is at no fault of the company. They have no control over weather or sighting of wildlife. Nevertheless, it was disappointing.

Tip: Leslie more or less runs the office by herself so I would recommend communicating with her via email rather than telephone. She is very busy and could be distracted on the phone especially during the day. She is very responsive and organize thou.

Review Text:
On our Alaska trip, one of the things I wanted to do more than anything else was to take a float-plane trip. I looked at the recommendations on Trip Advisor and started making arrangements for a booking.

Well, here's a tip. Don't wait until the last moment to book your float-plane trip. Not a good idea, as a lot of other people are wanting to take one of these trips just like you do. So, after finding one after the other companies being booked out I got a little disappointed. But, two of the other companies recommended SeaWind Aviation to me.

When I called Lesley (the owner's wife) she told me that they would have room for my wife and I to join them on our trip! Hooray! I booked it right then and there.

When we got to the docks, the folks from SeaWind were waiting for us. After a short trip to their base of operations, we headed to our plane with some new friends that we made on the docks. Watching the other planes take off in front of us (competitors) was very cool. We climbed into our DeHavilland aircraft and motored out into the bay. In a flash, we were airborne as the plane followed behind the others that had taken off earlier!

What a site to behold. Ketchikan from the air, the ships below, and the planes out ahead of us. Pretty soon, we were out of sight from Ketchikan and making our way into the Tongass National Forrest.

We had fantastic weather and every passenger had a seat with a window. One of the passengers, an Army veteran got to fly co-pilot and he was really jazzed about that. We all had head-sets to listen to our pilot Rolf narrate information about the sights below us. He was very knowledgeable about the landscape, the sights, and put us all at ease with his flying skills.

We landed on a lake out in the mountains and got out of the plane to stretch. While we were on the ground a bald eagle flew by and a small otter swam up to us looking for a treat. We got back into the plane and took off from the lake with a smooth takeoff.

I didn't want this trip to end, but alas, we made our way back toward Ketchikan and it was over.

The neat thing is that we were able to tour the town, since we took an early morning flight. We were not rushed, we had a ball and my wife is now hooked on small plane flight!

Thanks so much, SeaWind Aviation for a fantastic trip.

After getting briefed and strapped in, we took off on a magically warm and sunny day for a very smooth, unforgettable and fabulous tour of the Misty Fjords Monument.  During the entire flight, Steve gave us information of what we were seeing from the air.  He landed so smoothly on one of the pristine glacial lakes that it was hard to tell when we were on the water (a perfect 10), giving us the opportunity to get out of the plane and experience the monument's natural beauty from ground level. Wow!  Steve and Lesley are a perfect team for a seaplane tour operation. Review Title: Misty Fjords + Seawind Aviation = Breathtaking Tour
Review Text:
I took my wife on an Alaskan Cruise to celebrate her Big 5-0. We've been on several cruises before, but this was hands down the best ever! We took a helicopter out to the Mendenhall Glacier in Juneau, road the White Pass Summit and Yukon Railroad in Skagway, got rained on in Icy Strait Point (big surprise there!), and the highlight of the trip was the Misty Fjords National Monument flight with pilot Steve Kamm and Seawind Aviation! What a SPECTACULAR flight...the scenery was absolutely breathtaking!

I have to admit, I was a bit nervous...never been a fan of small planes...and to intentionally get into one that was going to take off and land in water was mind boggling! However, Steve is a real pro...the takeoff and landing was smoother than any plane I've ever been on...and I would fly with him again without hesitation.

Misty Fjords is simply an incredible experience, and the only way to truly experience this scenic gem is by seaplane. Steve provided great commentary and displayed his knowledge of the area, showed us all the sights including waterfalls and wildlife, and the water landing on the remote lake was just fantastic. Steve spotted a brown bear from the air, and landed the plane on the lake, turned off the engines, and paddled the plane real close to shore to keep from scaring the bear away, and we got an up close and personal view of a brown bear in his natural environment. Tremendous photo and video opportunity!

For those of you considering a Misty Fjords flightseeing tour, do yourself a favor...don't get ripped off by the cruise lines...book directly with Seawind. I called one night while I was out taking my dog for his evening stroll and spoke to Steve's wife Lesley. She answered all of my questions, and even gave me a military discount (I'm an Air Force vet). Seawind's prices are lower than their competitors...and WAY cheaper than the cruise line rates...and the deal was sweetened by the additional military discount. By the time I got back from the walk I had an email confirmation with all information, time, date, etc.. Once we arrived in Ketchikan, we were met at the pier and driven over to Seawind's office...less than 1 mile from the cruise ship dock...and before you knew it, we were zooming over the Misty Fjords National Monument! What an adventure...the highlight of our trip...and absolutely worth every penny!!!

But they did and Steve and Lesley were just as excited as we were. I know that they would have shared our disappointment too had we not seen anything.

I would highly highly recommend a trip with SeaWind Aviation. The booking was 100% smooth, they provided us with clear instructions as to the procedure when we arrived in port and where prompt in collecting us. In addition, we felt completely safe traveling with our 3 year old, 9 year old and 11 year old children. And if I haven't already made the point, Steve and Lesley are the kind of people you would like to make friends with!

Review Title: An experience not to be missed with a company you can trust.
Review Text: My sister and I booked our flight to Misty Fjords with Steve and Leslie Kamm following the glowing reports we had read on Trip Advisor. Review Text:
As part of our Alaska Inside Passage cruise, we were at Ketchikan during end of June 2011. We planned to do a 90 minutes float place flight into Misty Fiords but did not book anything in advance as Ketchikan weather can be very unpredictable. We booked our misty Fjords float plane trip when we arrived at Ketchikan. We booked with “SeaWind Aviation” which is a small family (husband & wife) run company. The name of the pilot was Steve and he is a cheerful kind of guy.

The weather was cloudy which is quite normal for Ketchikan and made the Fjords even more mysterious. I have never been to a float plane in the past and wasn’t sure what to expect. The take off was amazing and it took about 20 minutes to arrive at the Fjords. From air the area looked like a lost world. Steve, the pilot, spotted a bear and tried to show us the animal. But unfortunately I didn’t see any bear. Many people says a lot of good things about float planes but no one warned me about the fact that you will almost certainly get travel sickness and need to be prepared beforehand. I was feeling a bit sick after about 30 minutes and I was glad to be able to get out when the pilot landed the plane in a remote place within the Fjords.

The landing spot was simply amazing. It was middle of no where near a large rock within lake surrounded by vertical mountain rocks and forest around. It was damp, drizzly and misty and I’ll never forget the scenery and the experience. I must admit the Fjords looked much better from the ground; it was simply wonderful.

After about 15 minutes our flight took off again for more aerial view of the Fjords and eventually returned back to the base well after 90 minutes.

I haven’t flown with other companies and can’t tell what they are like.
However, I would strongly recommend this company for the way they made our experience truly memorable.

Review Title: Nice family company provide a beautiful way to see Alaska that's a great value.
Review Text:
Leslie was very helpful in setting up our reservation. I emailed her with my inquiries and she called me quickly to set everything up.

Seawind is definitely the best value that I could find anywhere for this type of tour. Because I had 7 people in my group (just what the plane holds minus the pilot), I was able to reserve the whole plane for $1,200. That is a great deal.

Leslie picked us up right at our ship and drove us to Seawind's dock. She was really nice.

We were up in the air quick. It was a really neat experience. The float plane is tiny, but comfortable. We flew over Misty Fjords for 45 minutes or so, then Steve landed us on an alpine lake and let us get out on a little island. Very serene and very fun. We walked around and took pictures for 15 minutes or so, then got back in the plane and flee back.

Steve spotted some mountain goats, so we flew right over them. Steve was a really nice guy. The only thing that would have been better would have been a little more commentary from him about what we were seeing.

Overall, though, it was a once in a lifetime kind of tour, and Seawind is cool family company that provides a great value.
